title: Keeping rabbits through winter
subtitle: Rabbits are hardier than most people think, but damp and draughts kill faster than frost.
excerpt: A healthy adult rabbit in a well-built hutch handles temperatures down to near freezing without difficulty. What causes problems in winter is wet bedding, inadequate water, and insufficient food energy. Here is how to set up the hutch, check daily, and adjust the feeding routine from November through March.
sourceNotes: British Rabbit Council welfare guidelines. RSPCA care notes for rabbits in cold weather. Carla Emery, Encyclopedia of Country Living (1994), notes on outdoor rabbit housing.

glossaryTerms.definition: The temperature at which moisture in the air condenses into liquid. Inside a poorly ventilated hutch in cold weather, condensation forms on surfaces and wets bedding even without rain getting in.

content.text: Rabbits do not thrive in heated indoor conditions any more than they do in waterlogged outdoor ones. A well-managed outdoor hutch is the right place for a healthy adult rabbit through the coldest months. Temperature is rarely the issue. What matters is ventilation to prevent
condensation and steady access to water and food.

Turn the hutch so the mesh front faces away from the prevailing wind and away from direct rain. On a north-facing wall of a shed or outbuilding is good, protected from wind and rain, with enough air movement to stop moisture building up inside.
Wrap the hutch on three sides with heavy-duty waterproof matting or a thick tarpaulin. Leave the front partially open for ventilation, sealing it shut creates a damp, airless box.
Pack the sleeping compartment with clean straw up to half-depth. Straw insulates; hay is for eating, not bedding, it holds moisture and moulds faster.
Raise the hutch off the ground on legs or a pallet if it is not already. Cold air pools at ground level and a waterlogged floor can wick cold up into the bedding.
Water bottles freeze before temperatures reach -2°C in windy conditions. Check the spout by tapping it every morning. A frozen bottle can lock a rabbit without water for hours without you noticing.

Two approaches: bring a second bottle indoors overnight and swap at the morning check, or fit an insulated bottle cover and check twice daily. A bowl of water as a backup works but spills and freezes faster than a bottle. Switch to a heavy ceramic bowl if you must, and check it at midday.

Rabbits burning more energy to stay warm need more food. Increase hay provision to unlimited, it should always be available, but in cold weather make sure the rack or hay net stays full. Increase pellet ration by around 10-15% from November through February.

Winter vegetables are fine as occasional extras but not as a primary feed. Frozen vegetables given straight from a cold store are likely to sit uneaten; bring them to room temperature first. Wet leafy greens given in bulk will freeze in the hutch if not eaten quickly and the rabbit may stop eating them.
Check water is flowing. Swap frozen bottle or top up bowl.
Check the rabbit is active and interested in food. A rabbit sitting hunched at the back of the sleeping compartment, not moving when you open the door, needs hands-on assessment for illness.
Remove wet or soiled bedding. Damp straw in contact with the rabbit drops body temperature faster than cold air. Add fresh dry straw to maintain insulation depth.
Top up hay rack and pellets.

attrs.cue: Rabbit not eating or drinking for more than half a day
attrs.cause: Illness, gut stasis, or pain from a cold-related injury
attrs.fix: Bring the rabbit indoors to a warm room and check for signs of gut stasis: hard abdomen, no droppings, teeth-grinding. No gut sounds on gentle ear-to-belly listening is a vet call.

attrs.cue: Bedding damp even after removal and replacement
attrs.cause: Condensation from poor ventilation, or rain getting in through a gap
attrs.fix: Check hutch roof and sides for leaks. Improve front ventilation: a solid-fronted hutch in winter is as damaging as a draughty one. Consider moving indoors to a shed if it cannot be made dry.

attrs.cue: Ears are cold to the touch and rabbit is limp
attrs.fix: Bring inside immediately, warm gradually in a towel at room temperature. Do not use a hot water bottle directly on the skin. Vet call once stable if recovery is slow.
